subject: Vulnerability management - 90-day CVE closure & scan cadence certification
messages:
From: Joan Park <security@acme-corp.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Mark Lin <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: VM evidence & SLA commitment for SOC2 review

Diego,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our SOC 2 readiness review we need explicit evidence on Redwood's vulnerability management cadence and remediation SLAs. Specifically Acme needs:

- A documented scan cadence (frequency per asset class) for both internal infra and customer-facing services.
- Target SLAs for CVE remediation by severity (critical/high/medium) and an escalation path.
- Evidence of recent scan results (last 90 days) and confirmation that open critical CVEs are being closed within your stated SLAs.
- A signed attestation committing to a 90-day closure window for newly discovered critical CVEs, and point of contact for audit follow-up.

Attachments are fine as links or PDFs. Can you get this to us by EOD 2027-05-04? Procurement will need it for the legal packet.

Appreciate it —
Joan Park
Director, Security Assurance
Acme Cloud Apps

[Attachment: acme-soc2-checklist.xlsx (referenced)]

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Joan Park <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Mark Lin <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence & SLA commitment for SOC2 review

Joan —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide the artifacts and a signed attestation. High-level summary below; I attached the artifacts referenced. Full attestation draft will follow from Marissa by EOD.

Summary: 
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated credentialed scans for customer-facing endpoints; bi-weekly host-level scans for infra; monthly full external penetration assessment. See attached weekly-scan-schedule.csv for mapping by asset group.
- CVE remediation SLAs (we commit): Critical = 90 days from disclosure in customer environment (exceptions require documented compensating controls and SLA extension approval), High = 180 days, Medium = 365 days. See cve-remediation-sla-matrix.pdf for full definitions and escalation ladders.
- Evidence: exported scan runs from the last 90 days are included (redacted as appropriate). Open criticals are tagged and routed to our Rapid Remediation queue; we have a 72-hour triage window before active remediation starts.
- Audit contact / escalation: laura_bennett@redwood.com (Security Ops), and I will serve as customer liaison for procurement/legal.

Attached: weekly-scan-schedule.csv, cve-remediation-sla-matrix.pdf, vm-runbook.md

Next steps: Marissa will provide the attestation language. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer to review the SLA table line-by-line.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198

[Attachment stubs included above]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Joan Park <security@acme-corp.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Mark Lin <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Draft attestation: 90-day critical CVE closure commitment

Hi Joan —

Per Diego's note, please find the attestation draft below. We've kept the language narrow to satisfy audit requirements while preserving operational exceptions. If this looks good we'll prepare a signed PDF.

--- Attestation (draft) ---
Redwood Inference hereby attests that for customer-impacting critical vulnerabilities discovered in Redwood-managed inference environments, Redwood will: 
1) Acknowledge and triage the vulnerability within 72 hours of discovery;
2) Implement remediation or an approved mitigation within 90 calendar days of discovery, except where an approved exception is documented and communicated to the customer;
3) Maintain records of triage, mitigation steps, and closure evidence available for audit for at least 24 months.

This attestation covers hosted and dedicated deployment modes; private deployments where the customer controls patching may have different timelines and are handled via contract language.

--- end draft ---

Can you confirm acceptance or provide edits? If accepted, we will sign and return as a PDF by 2027-05-04.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: attestation-draft.txt (inline)]

From: Joan Park <security@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Mark Lin <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft attestation: 90-day critical CVE closure commitment

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear draft. Acme accepts this language with one small edit: please add that for critical CVEs affecting customer-data-plane endpoints, Redwood will provide weekly status updates until closure. Otherwise the timeline is acceptable.

Procurement (Mark) requests the signed attestation be delivered with a deliverable link for our legal packet (DocuSign preferred).

Can you confirm you'll include the weekly status update clause and send a signed copy?

Regards,
Joan Park
Director, Security Assurance
Acme Cloud Apps
